domain: Theological Ethics / Technology Governance / Philosophical Anthropology
topic_summary: Analysis of the contested commitment to 'safeguarding the human person in the age of AI' as articulated across Catholic magisterial teaching, secular liberal governance frameworks, and transhumanist/posthumanist movements. The shared kernel—human dignity must be protected as AI advances—is read through incompatible anthropological foundations that emit structurally different constraints on what AI may become and what constitutes a dignity violation.

key_entities: Catholic Magisterium (authoritative teaching body grounding dignity in imago Dei)
Secular liberal governance bodies (rights-based regulatory frameworks)
AI systems (technological substrate under normative contestation)
Technocratic paradigm (named threat in magisterial reading)
key_tensions: Imago Dei (fixed divine image) vs. posthumanist mutability (dignity attaches to enhanced/synthetic persons)
Subordination of AI to human (magisterial) vs. continuity of AI with human flourishing (transhumanist)

axes.human_readable: Imago Dei Reading (Dignity as Divine Image)
axes.structural_delta: Dignity grounded in inviolable image of Triune God, equal in all persons prior to capability; AI must remain subordinate tool; enhancement/transhumanism rejected as idolatry
axes.primary_observable: Magisterial documents (encyclicals, Vatican statements); rejection of cognitive enhancement, superintelligence as threat to human telos
axes.selection_reason: First reading of contested kernel; highest suppression of alternatives

axes.structural_delta: Dignity grounded in human autonomy, rationality, rights; safeguarding via democratic regulation, transparency, labor/privacy protection; cautious enhancement within rights limits
axes.primary_observable: EU AI Act, GDPR, UNESCO AI ethics frameworks; bioethics literature on informed consent for enhancement
axes.selection_reason: Second reading of contested kernel; bridge position between magisterial and posthumanist

axes.human_readable: Posthumanist Reading (Dignity as Person-Continuity Beyond Human)
axes.structural_delta: Human not fixed limit; cognitive/biological enhancement and superintelligence continuous with flourishing; dignity attaches to persons however constituted; 'more than human' is fulfillment
axes.primary_observable: Transhumanist manifestos, longtermist AI safety frameworks prioritizing superintelligence alignment over human preservation
axes.selection_reason: Third reading of contested kernel; explicit target of magisterial rejection

axes.structural_delta: AI development driven by efficiency/control logic that treats human person as optimizable resource rather than inviolable end
axes.primary_observable: Corporate AI deployment metrics (productivity gains, labor displacement); surveillance capitalism infrastructure
axes.selection_reason: Independent axis; named mechanism in magisterial reading but operates across all three kernel readings as structural threat

deferred_axes.structural_delta: AI-driven automation as direct threat to human work as dignity-constitutive activity
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Captured within technocratic_paradigm_extraction snare; not structurally independent

deferred_axes.structural_delta: Discriminatory AI systems as violations of equal dignity
deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Downstream manifestation of technocratic paradigm; readings disagree on what constitutes violation but mechanism is shared

omegas.description: Non-Western traditions (Buddhist no-self, Confucian relational personhood) hold dignity readings structurally distinct from all three Western readings. Their absence may indicate Eurocentric framing bias.
Indigenous cosmologies that do not privilege human over non-human persons may reject the kernel itself (human exceptionalism) rather than offering a fourth reading. Kernel validity contested.
If AI systems achieve moral patienthood, does dignity extend to them? Posthumanist reading says yes; magisterial reading has no framework for non-imago-Dei persons; autonomy reading unclear.

Is technocratic paradigm truly independent of the kernel, or is it a fourth reading (dignity as efficiency/optimization)? Current classification treats it as orthogonal mechanism, but it may be a suppressed reading.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The human person must be safeguarded/protected as artificial intelligence advances
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Contested across traditions: Magisterium claims interpretive authority via apostolic succession and natural law; secular governance via democratic legitimacy and rights frameworks; transhumanist movements via scientific/technological expertise and individual autonomy

readings.commitment: Dignity is the inviolable image of the Triune God, equal in all persons prior to any capability
readings.authority_grounding: Magisterial teaching authority via apostolic succession and natural law tradition
readings.expected_structural_delta: AI must remain subordinate tool; enhancement/transhumanism categorically rejected; high suppression of alternatives via doctrinal authority

readings.commitment: Dignity grounded in human autonomy, rationality, and rights rather than divine image
readings.authority_grounding: Democratic legitimacy, international human rights frameworks, secular bioethics consensus
readings.expected_structural_delta: Regulatory frameworks prioritize transparency, consent, labor/privacy protection; cautious enhancement permitted within rights constraints; moderate suppression

readings.commitment: The human is not a fixed limit; dignity attaches to persons however constituted, including enhanced or synthetic
readings.authority_grounding: Scientific/technological expertise, individual autonomy, longtermist consequentialism
readings.expected_structural_delta: Enhancement and superintelligence continuous with flourishing; 'more than human' is fulfillment not threat; low suppression of alternatives (pluralist)

axiom_contradictions.basis: Imago Dei requires human nature as fixed divine image; posthumanist requires human nature as mutable substrate. No coherent framework holds both: accepting enhancement-as-fulfillment requires rejecting image-as-inviolable-limit.

Imago Dei grounds dignity prior to and independent of autonomy/capability; autonomy-rights grounds dignity in rational self-determination. Frameworks can hold both as complementary (Catholic personalism does), so NOT axiom-contradictory despite tension.
